bun-bo-cay-bac-lieu.name: Bac Lieu spicy beef rice noodles
bun-bo-cay-bac-lieu.serving_basis: Four medium bowls with spicy broth, beef and Thai basil; adjust the satay to taste.
bun-bo-cay-bac-lieu.description: Bac Lieu spicy beef bún is known for its deep golden broth, the fragrant heat of satay and tender beef served with white rice vermicelli. Bếp Việt adapts a home batch with a lighter broth, keeping Thai basil, lime and chili salt as characteristic accompaniments.
bun-bo-cay-bac-lieu.finished_dish: A hot bowl of naturally golden-orange broth, tender but distinct beef slices, white vermicelli and fragrant Thai basil; add satay and chili separately to control the heat.
bun-bo-cay-bac-lieu.serving: Briefly blanch the noodles, arrange the beef and ladle over simmering broth. Serve with Thai basil, lime and chili salt; let each person add satay at the table.
tips: Blanch the bones and beef briefly, then rinse them to reduce scum and odor in the broth.
Fry the satay gently and use enough for aroma and color without letting the chili burn.
Remove the beef as soon as tender, cool slightly and slice across the grain; keep the broth at a gentle simmer.
bun-bo-cay-bac-lieu.image_alt: Bac Lieu spicy beef bún in a white ceramic bowl with rice vermicelli, beef, golden-red broth, Thai basil and lime; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
bun-bo-cay-bac-lieu.time_note: About 2 hours 15 minutes, mostly for simmering the bones and tenderizing the beef.

ingredients.name: Sugar

ingredients.name: Cooking oil

ingredients.name: Water

ingredients.name: Thai basil

ingredients.name: Limes

ingredients.name: Fresh chili

preparation_steps: Rinse the bones and beef. Blanch separately for three minutes, discard the water and rinse away any scum.
Bruise the lemongrass and mince the shallots and garlic. Wash the basil, limes and chili, then drain.
Set up the broth pot and keep separate utensils for raw and cooked beef to avoid cross-contamination.
cooking_steps: Add the bones, beef shank, lemongrass and water to a pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 75–90 minutes until the beef is tender.
Transfer the beef to a clean plate, cool slightly and slice across the grain. Simmer the bones for another 15 minutes, then strain or remove the bones and lemongrass.
Fry the shallots, garlic and minced lemongrass in oil. Add satay and stir briefly over low heat; add annatto oil if using, then loosen with a ladle of broth.
Pour the satay mixture into the pot and season with fish sauce, salt and sugar. Simmer for five minutes, taste and adjust the heat.
Briefly blanch the vermicelli, divide it among bowls, add the beef and ladle over very hot broth. Serve at once with Thai basil, lime and chili salt.

banh-chung-den-lang-son.name: Lang Son black bánh chưng
aliases: Black bánh chưng from Xu Lang
banh-chung-den-lang-son.serving_basis: One family-sized square cake cut into eight pieces; serve warm or pan-fry after refrigeration.
banh-chung-den-lang-son.description: Lang Son black bánh chưng is a Tay variation: glutinous rice is soaked in carefully filtered plant-ash water, then wrapped with mung beans and pork in dong leaves. Bếp Việt adapts a family batch; use only ash water confirmed safe for food and never burn unknown plants to make it.
banh-chung-den-lang-son.finished_dish: A square cake with glossy dark glutinous rice, a nutty yellow mung-bean layer and tender pork; the color comes from the rice treatment, not charring.
banh-chung-den-lang-son.serving: Let the cake rest after boiling, press it lightly to drain, then slice with a clean knife. Serve with pickled onions or vegetables; refrigerate leftovers promptly and reheat thoroughly.
tips: Use only plant-ash water labeled or confirmed for food use; do not use ash from unidentified plants, contaminated materials or chemical-treated wood.
Soak the rice and mung beans separately and distribute the filling evenly so the center cooks through.
Keep the cake submerged during boiling, top up with boiling water and maintain a gentle boil; never let the pot run dry.
cooking_method: soaking rice in food-grade ash water
search_terms: black glutinous rice cake with mung bean and pork
banh-chung-den-lang-son.image_alt: Lang Son black bánh chưng wrapped in green dong leaves, with a cut piece showing dark rice, mung beans and pork; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-chung-den-lang-son.time_note: About 20 hours, including eight hours of soaking and 10–12 hours of boiling; the rice can soak overnight.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse and soak in filtered food-grade ash water.

ingredients.name: Filtered food-grade plant-ash water
ingredients.notes: Use only a product confirmed safe for food and dilute as directed.

ingredients.name: Split mung beans
ingredients.notes: Soak, steam until tender and mash coarsely.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Cut into strips for the filling; avoid an overly lean piece.

ingredients.name: Shallots

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide among the rice, beans and pork.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the pork filling.

ingredients.name: Dong leaves
ingredients.notes: Choose wide leaves, wash and soften over gentle heat.

ingredients.name: Bamboo ties
ingredients.notes: Soak until pliable before wrapping.

ingredients.name: Boiling water
ingredients.notes: Keep the cakes covered and top up with boiling water as needed.

preparation_steps: Rinse the glutinous rice and soak for eight hours in filtered food-grade ash water prepared according to its supplier's directions. Drain; do not make ash water from unidentified plants.
Soak the mung beans until soft, steam and mash coarsely. Season the pork with shallots, pepper and some salt.
Wash and gently warm the dong leaves until pliable, then wipe dry. Soak the ties and prepare a tall pot that can hold the cake flat.
cooking_steps: Mix the drained rice with the remaining salt. Divide the rice, mung beans and pork into even portions for one square cake.
Line the mold with dong leaves, add rice, mung beans and pork in centered layers, then cover with rice. Fold into a square and tie firmly without compressing it too tightly.
Place the cake in a pot and cover it with at least 3–4 cm of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10–12 hours, adding boiling water to keep it submerged.
Lift out the cake, rinse the outside of the leaves and drain. Press gently for two to three hours, then cool before slicing; refrigerate leftovers.

banh-tom-ho-tay-ha-noi.name: Hồ Tây shrimp cakes
banh-tom-ho-tay-ha-noi.serving_basis: About eight small cakes, two per person, served hot with fresh greens and sweet-sour dipping sauce.
banh-tom-ho-tay-ha-noi.description: Hồ Tây shrimp cakes are associated with Hanoi's West Lake area: fresh shrimp and sweet-potato strands are coated in a light batter and fried until golden. Bếp Việt adapts a home batch with just enough batter to hold the cake together, serving the shrimp whole with greens, pickles and sweet-sour fish sauce.
banh-tom-ho-tay-ha-noi.finished_dish: Thin golden cakes with pink shrimp visible on top and fragrant sweet potato; fresh greens and pickles balance the richness of the fried batter.
banh-tom-ho-tay-ha-noi.serving: Drain the cakes on a rack or absorbent paper and serve hot. Wrap with lettuce and herbs, add pickles and dip in sweet-sour fish sauce; do not cover the hot cakes, or steam will soften them.
tips: Cut the sweet potato into short strands and pat dry so the batter holds and fries evenly.
Use only enough batter to coat the ingredients; keep the cakes thin rather than forming a thick pancake.
Keep the oil at a steady medium heat and fry in small batches; drain the cakes as soon as they come out.
banh-tom-ho-tay-ha-noi.image_alt: Golden Hồ Tây shrimp cakes topped with whole shrimp and sweet-potato strands, served with fresh greens and dipping sauce; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-tom-ho-tay-ha-noi.time_note: About 1 hour 5 minutes, including ten minutes to rest the batter and make quick pickles.

ingredients.name: Small fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh shrimp; keep the shell if thin, rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Sweet potato
ingredients.notes: Peel, cut into short strands and pat dry.

ingredients.name: Wheat flour
ingredients.notes: Sift before use.

ingredients.name: Cold water

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the batter.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For deep-frying; the amount depends on the pot diameter.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: For the dip; adjust for saltiness.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: For the sweet-sour dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Add after the sugar dissolves.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Mince for the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Shred thinly for quick pickles.

ingredients.name: Daikon
ingredients.notes: Shred thinly for quick pickles.

ingredients.name: Lettuce and fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Wash well and drain completely.

preparation_steps: Rinse the shrimp under cold water, trim long antennae if needed and drain. Peel the sweet potato, cut into short strands and pat dry with a clean towel.
Shred the carrot and daikon. Wash the fresh greens and drain thoroughly.
Dissolve the sugar in fish sauce and 60 ml warm water; add lime juice, garlic and chili. Toss the carrot and daikon with some of the sauce and rest for ten minutes.
Whisk the flours and salt. Beat the duck egg with cold water and gradually stir it into the flour until just thick enough to coat; rest for ten minutes.
cooking_steps: Fold the sweet potato into the batter. Heat the oil over medium heat; test with a drop of batter, which should rise and sizzle evenly without darkening at once.
Scoop a portion of the coated potato into a small frying ladle and spread it thinly. Arrange two or three shrimp on top, lower gently into the oil and fry in batches.
Fry for about three to four minutes per side, turning once when the edges set and turn golden. The shrimp should be fully opaque and pink; drain the cakes on a rack.
Serve hot with greens, pickles and the remaining dipping sauce. Keep children away from the hot oil.

banh-canh-trang-bang-tay-ninh.name: Trảng Bàng bánh canh
aliases: Trảng Bàng bánh canh Tây Ninh
banh-canh-trang-bang-tay-ninh.serving_basis: Four bowls with rice-flour noodles, boiled pork and seasonal greens; divide the pork hock to taste.
banh-canh-trang-bang-tay-ninh.description: Trảng Bàng bánh canh is a Tay Ninh noodle soup made with thick rice-flour noodles, a clear pork broth, boiled pork and wild greens on the side. Bếp Việt adapts a home version with ready-made fresh noodles; choose seasonal greens such as herbs, perilla, fish mint and mildly sour leaves.
banh-canh-trang-bang-tay-ninh.finished_dish: A bowl of light broth with soft, springy rice noodles, tender pork and pork hock; fresh greens balance the broth's gentle savory richness.
banh-canh-trang-bang-tay-ninh.serving: Blanch the noodles separately, ladle over hot broth and top with sliced pork and hock. Serve with seasonal wild greens, lime, chili and a small dish of pepper fish sauce for the pork.
tips: Blanch the bones and pork first, rinse well, then simmer to keep the broth clear and mild.
Lift the pork out as soon as it is tender; leaving it in the pot too long can make the slices dry and crumbly.
Cook the noodles according to their package directions; rinse briefly if heavily dusted with starch before adding broth.
banh-canh-trang-bang-tay-ninh.image_alt: A bowl of Trảng Bàng bánh canh with rice-flour noodles, boiled pork, pork hock, herbs and a small pepper-fish-sauce dip; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-canh-trang-bang-tay-ninh.time_note: About 2 hours 20 minutes, mostly to simmer the bones and cook the pork.

ingredients.name: Pork shoulder

ingredients.name: Pork hock

ingredients.name: Fresh rice bánh canh noodles

ingredients.name: Yellow onion

ingredients.name: Shallots

ingredients.name: Rock sugar

ingredients.name: Black pepper

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the broth; add hot water if needed.

ingredients.name: Seasonal fresh greens and herbs

ingredients.name: Limes

ingredients.name: Fresh chili

preparation_steps: Blanch the bones, pork shoulder and hock in boiling water for three minutes. Discard the water and rinse away scum.
Lightly char the yellow onion and shallots. Wash the greens and drain; prepare the lime, chili and pepper.
Read the package directions for the bánh canh noodles; if fresh noodles carry excess starch, rinse briefly after blanching.
cooking_steps: Add the bones, water, charred onion and half the salt to a pot. Bring to a boil, skim and simmer gently for 75–90 minutes.
Cook the pork shoulder and hock in the broth until tender, lifting each piece out as soon as it is done. Cool slightly and slice the shoulder.
Strain the broth and season with fish sauce, remaining salt, pepper and optional rock sugar. Keep it at a gentle simmer.
Blanch the noodles separately until tender and springy, then divide among bowls. Arrange the pork and hock, ladle over hot broth and serve with greens, lime, chili and pepper fish sauce.

chao-luon-vinh-nghe-an.name: Vinh eel porridge, Nghe An
chao-luon-vinh-nghe-an.serving_basis: Four bowls of thick porridge topped with separately sautéed eel, herbs and chili to taste; serve with bánh mướt or bread if desired.
chao-luon-vinh-nghe-an.description: Vinh eel porridge is a specialty of Nghe An, pairing slowly cooked rice porridge with field eel sautéed in turmeric, local shallots and chili. Bếp Việt adapts a home method that keeps the eel pieces intact, uses carefully strained eel-bone stock and lets each diner adjust the heat.
chao-luon-vinh-nghe-an.finished_dish: Golden, thick porridge with softened but distinct rice grains, turmeric-scented eel on top, and rau răm, rice-paddy herb and pepper for a warming finish.
chao-luon-vinh-nghe-an.serving: Ladle hot porridge into bowls and top with the sautéed eel. Scatter rau răm, rice-paddy herb, scallions and pepper. Serve with bánh mướt or bread and add extra chili if desired.
tips: Strain the eel-bone stock through a fine sieve so no small bones remain in the porridge.
Simmer the rice gently and avoid vigorous stirring so the grains open without breaking into paste.
Sauté the eel separately with turmeric and local shallots, stirring only as needed so the pieces stay whole and moist.
chao-luon-vinh-nghe-an.image_alt: A bowl of golden Vinh eel porridge with sautéed field eel, scallions, rau răm, rice-paddy herb and fried shallots; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
chao-luon-vinh-nghe-an.time_note: About 1 hour 50 minutes, including eel preparation, stock and porridge simmering.

ingredients.name: Cleaned field eel
ingredients.notes: Buy from a trusted supplier; check that slime, viscera and clotted blood have been removed.

ingredients.name: Long-grain rice

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse with the long-grain rice for a slightly thicker porridge.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the porridge; add hot water if it thickens too much.

ingredients.name: Local shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and bruise or mince; substitute shallots if unavailable.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Mince for sautéing.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Bruise and use to poach the eel.

ingredients.name: Fresh turmeric
ingredients.notes: Pound or mince; substitute a small amount of ground turmeric if needed.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Remove seeds or reduce for less heat.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the eel and the porridge separately.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between poaching and porridge.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the shallots and sautéing the eel.

ingredients.name: Rau răm
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Rice-paddy herb
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Slice finely.

ingredients.name: Ground pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle before serving.

preparation_steps: If the eel is not pre-cleaned, ask the fishmonger to prepare it or use suitable tools to remove slime; do not handle raw eel bare-handed over cooked-food surfaces. Rinse and keep separate.
Rinse the long-grain and glutinous rice gently. Bruise the ginger; mince the local shallots, shallots and turmeric. Wash and slice the herbs and scallions.
Prepare a fine sieve and a clean plate for the cooked eel. Wash tools that touched raw eel before using them again.
cooking_steps: Poach the eel with ginger, a little salt and enough water to cover until fully cooked. Transfer it to a clean plate, remove the flesh along the backbone and keep the backbone.
Crush or finely chop the backbone, return it to the poaching liquid and simmer for 15 minutes. Strain carefully through a fine sieve and discard all bone fragments.
Add the strained stock to a pot with both kinds of rice. Simmer gently for 40–50 minutes until the grains open and the porridge thickens; stir lightly with a ladle as needed.
Fry the local shallots and shallots in oil. Add the turmeric and chili, stir until fragrant, then add eel, fish sauce and a little salt. Sauté briefly until the eel is hot and seasoned.
Taste the porridge, ladle into bowls and top with the sautéed eel. Add rau răm, rice-paddy herb, scallions and pepper; serve hot with bánh mướt or bread.
